cultural.vision_reason: This is a model of a Haida mortuary box/tomb on pillars, carved and painted with a classic Haida formline crest design (bear face with characteristic ovoid eyes and formline elements) — a recognized Haida architectural/funerary form.

physical.title: model building/structure; tomb
physical.summary:
Model of a Haida tomb consisting of a rectangular pine wood box (a) held between two wooden pillars stained dark brown. The front of the rectangle is decorated in relief by a crest depicting a formline bear's head and front paws with protruding tounge and incisors. The head is painted with blue, black and red paint and a red line runs along the bottom edge of the front panel. The rear panel is an undecorated rectangle of loose wood. The lid (b) is largely rectangular with two rounded bulges at either end stained, like the pillars, dark brown. The front edge of the lid is painted red and inlaid with six squares of haliotis shell. 

The model tomb was designed to contain two almost identical model Haida box coffins (see records for Am1902,0526.1.c-e and f-h) which each contain small wooden effigies of deceased Haida.
